title: Diwali Party Season Is Here: A Skin-Smart Game Plan for the Card Parties
excerpt: With Diwali falling on November 8, the card-party circuit stretches across five weeks — dermatologists and beauty writers say a glowing festive look is built with a two-week prep plan, not a last-minute dash.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 this year — about five weeks out — so the card-party circuit is already warming up, and this is the ideal window to start a pre-festival skincare plan rather than a last-minute sprint.
  • Start now: exfoliate 2–3 times a week with a gentle AHA (5–10% glycolic acid is well-studied for evening tone; mandelic acid if sensitive) and apply only one new active product at a time — ten days is the minimum buffer before the big events.
  • Party-week essentials: apply hyaluronic acid to damp skin within 60 seconds of washing, seal with a ceramide moisturizer, use SPF 30+ and reapply every 2–3 hours outdoors, and never sleep in makeup — oil-cleanse, then wash.
  • Eat for glow: seasonal pomegranates, oranges and papaya for vitamin C; almonds, cashews and sunflower seeds for healthy fats; and plenty of water — enjoy the mithai, just pair it with intention.

The invitations are going out, the guest lists are being drawn up, and the Diwali card-party season is officially underway. With the festival falling on Sunday, November 8 this year — pushed unusually late by the Adhik Maas — the RSVP calendar is stretching across five full weeks of dinners, taash parties, office celebrations, and pujas.

The Times of India captured the mood this week: Diwali party season is here, and the question on everyone's mind is who is RSVPing — and how everyone plans to look when they arrive. Between fireworks smoke, late nights, heavy makeup, and indulgent spreads, the festive season is notoriously hard on skin. But dermatologists and beauty writers agree on one thing: a glowing Diwali look is built weeks ahead, not bought the night before.

Five weeks out: start the prep, not the panic

The quiet fortnight is your friend. Lifestyle Asia India's festive skincare guide lays out a simple, no-fuss routine that works: cleanse gently twice a day (fireworks and smog clog pores fast), exfoliate 2–3 times a week with a gentle chemical or enzyme exfoliant — a homemade besan-turmeric-curd ubtan counts — and keep moisturizing consistently. As one widely-circulated festive skincare timeline puts it: week one is about clearing the backlog with a leave-on AHA like 5–10% glycolic acid, used two or three times across the week; week two is about rebuilding the barrier with ceramides and hyaluronic acid.

One rule dominates every dermatologist-approved guide: do not start a new active three days before Diwali. Retinol, new vitamin C serums, and strong acids need ten days of lead time, or you risk arriving at the party mid-purge. One new product, used consistently, is enough.

Party-week survival

Once the invitations start overlapping, the priorities shift from treatment to defense. HealthShots' dermatologist-backed guide recommends a lightweight vitamin C or niacinamide serum under SPF 30+ sunscreen every morning — pollution and firework smoke generate free radicals that dull skin, and antioxidants neutralize them. Apply sunscreen at least 15 minutes before stepping out and reapply every 2–3 hours if you're out for daytime events or shopping.

For the evenings, the golden rule is non-negotiable: never sleep with makeup on. Use an oil-based cleanser or micellar water, then your regular face wash — a dab of almond or coconut oil on a cotton pad dissolves heavy eye makeup while nourishing the under-eye area. A hydrating sheet mask or a sandalwood-and-rosewater paste twice a week makes a quick pre-event refresh, and a multani mitti (Fuller's earth) mask with saffron strands cools and brightens after long smoky nights.

The diaspora party circuit

For the diaspora, the RSVP question hits differently — Diwali season in the US and UK means office parties, temple events, and community galas, often in centrally heated rooms that dehydrate skin fast. Keep a rose-water or cucumber face mist in your bag for a quick refresh between venues, and remember that UVA rays pass through windows, so indoor daylight hours still call for sunscreen. The good news: with Diwali on a Sunday this year, the post-festival weekend doubles as recovery time.

What's next

Dhanteras kicks off the five-day festival on Friday, November 6, followed by Choti Diwali, the main Lakshmi Puja on November 8, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj on November 10. That leaves roughly four solid weeks of prep — more than enough for the two-week timeline to work its magic. Start the exfoliation now, lock in the barrier next week, and the only thing left to worry about is the guest list.
